site_name: Colossus 2 (Tulane Road, Whitehaven, Memphis)
serving_utility: Memphis Light, Gas and Water (MLGW; TVA wholesale) is the territorial utility, but the site has run mainly on operator-owned gas turbines across the state line in Southaven, MS
load_basis: Epoch AI estimate: 239 MW IT power at 19 Oct 2025, unchanged at 13 Jan 2026 (first cluster, ~110,000 GB200 processors, ~210 MW of compute). Satellite/disclosure-based estimate, not a utility figure.
notes: MLGW's 5 May 2025 public update says the Tulane Rd site sits next to a large TVA/MLGW substation, that xAI had made an initial 260 MW grid request (range of 260 MW to 1.1 GW discussed) but had NOT submitted a final request, no system impact study had started, and the site was 'not consuming significant electricity'. Wikipedia and Epoch describe power as relying heavily on a gas-turbine plant on the former Duke Energy site in Southaven, MS (69 temporary turbines; 1.2 GW permanent plant permitted March 2026). I found no later document confirming how much MLGW grid power is delivered, so treat MLGW as the territorial utility with behind-the-meter generation carrying most of the load; utility confidence is low. Our 946 MW figure is Epoch's June 2026 estimate, not a 2025 figure (Epoch: 239 MW Oct 2025 and Jan 2026, 490 MW Apr 2026, 946 MW Jun 2026, 1,531 MW projected Feb 2027). Year: Epoch dates the first cluster online by 19 Oct 2025; Wikipedia says 'around January 2026' without a citation. Lat/lon not independently verified. site_name: Amazon (AWS) Susquehanna campus, formerly Cumulus Data (Talen), Berwick/Salem Township
serving_utility: None through 2025: power delivered directly from Talen Energy's adjacent Susquehanna nuclear plant (co-located, behind the meter). PPL Electric Utilities becomes the delivery utility, with Talen as retail supplier, after a reconfiguration scheduled for spring 2026
load_basis: Ceiling, not metered load: 'existing 300-MW' behind-the-meter co-location arrangement between Talen and AWS (FERC rejected raising it to 480 MW in Nov 2024). Actual 2025 draw not found.
notes: Our PPL assignment is wrong for the years through 2025: the campus took power directly from Susquehanna under a 300 MW co-location arrangement. The June 2025 Talen-Amazon deal (1,920 MW through 2042; 840-1,200 MW in 2029, 1,680-1,920 MW in 2032) moves it front-of-the-meter, with PPL Electric handling transmission and delivery and Talen as the licensed retail supplier; POWER says the switch was to happen during the spring 2026 refueling outage. I did not confirm that the switch actually occurred. Year: Wikipedia, citing a Talen release of 17 Jan 2023, says Cumulus finished phase 1 construction on that date (the original release URL now redirects to Talen's IR home page); first commercial load date not found, so 2023 is the construction-complete year. Talen sold the campus to AWS on 4 Mar 2024.
